correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge1\) and prime-power field size \(q\), Lie generation is equivalent to the two projected subspaces spanning the \(2n\)-dimensional symplectic quotient. The centrally containing population is in bijection with all quotient subspaces, and the probability of the noncentral isotropic graph population is \(O_q((n+1)q^{-n^2/3+n+3/8})\). For fixed dimension offsets \(n+j,n+k\) the spanning kernel is exactly \(\Phi_{n+j}\Phi_{n+k}/(\Phi_{j+k}\Phi_{2n})\) when \(j+k\ge0\) and zero otherwise. Gaussian-binomial tail estimates justify both the theta double series and \(O_q(q^{-n/2})\) convergence. Standalone exhaustive checks count 77, 7925, and 203195 generating pairs in the named small configurations and numerically test twelve growing-rank finite sums; the computations corroborate, rather than replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The precise new theorem concerns two uniformly sampled subalgebras generating the entire growing Heisenberg Lie algebra, with an explicit nontrivial theta-mixture limit and exponential fixed-field error. The closest inspected exact Heisenberg census and nonpermuting-pair formula do not determine the incidence of a pair of projections spanning their quotient; a separate published Grassmann note controls fixed-rank disjointness, and Glasby et al. impose fixed-rank nondegeneracy. The new statement requires the Lie-generation equivalence, mixing all dimensions, and uniform asymptotic control. Existing numerical and single-subalgebra results are explicitly credited, and implicit broader coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older theorem about two random all-dimension finite-field subspaces might already evaluate this double theta mixture, possibly under random vector-space generation terminology.
The limiting expression is a nontrivial synthesis of classical Gaussian and subalgebra counts; a prior source could contain the equivalent synthesis even without Lie terminology.
Some potential group-side analogues and publisher-only background sources were not inspected in full; independence or publication priority is not certified.
The 2021 complementary-subspace formula is an exact kernel specialization; another paper may have already summed it over all dimensions.

value.rationale: Pairwise generation is a natural algebraic invariant that differs essentially from previously studied permutability. The theta-mixture limiting probability is strictly between zero and one for every fixed field and quantifies its dependence on q; the result also shows a strong universality transfer from a nonlinear Lie-subalgebra ensemble to ordinary random subspaces with superexponential error. The numerical constants 0.3097 at \(q=2\) and 0.4853 at \(q=3\) exhibit genuine nondegenerate behavior. This is a meaningful full-family asymptotic rather than an arbitrary isolated finite parameter.
